chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Al-Fadl ibn al-Saqr al-Abdi narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated from al-A'mash, from Ubaya ibn Rib'i, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

I am the Master of the Prophets, and Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Master of the Trustees. And indeed, my trustees after me are twelve, the first of them is Ali ibn Abi Talib and the last of them is the Riser (al-Qa'im).
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve trustees (awsiya) succeeding the Prophet according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* establishes the Imamate as a divinely appointed succession, linking the Prophet’s authority directly to Ali and the subsequent twelve Imams. It serves as a foundational proof for the Twelver doctrine, explicitly identifying Ali as the first trustee and al-Qa'im (the Mahdi) as the final one, thereby confirming the continuity of spiritual and political leadership.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-31 Ahmad ibn Al-Hassan al-Qattan narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya bin Zakariya al-Qattan quoted on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Fadhl ibn al-Saqr al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Mo’awiya, on the authority of al-A’amesh, on the authority of Abaya ibn Reb’ee, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas that God’s Prophet (s) said, “

I am the Master of the Prophets, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (s) is the Master of the Trustees. The Trustees after me are twelve, the first of whom is Ali ibn Abi Talib (s) and their last one is the Riser.”
